$description: A source-neutral reference for the friendly, plain-spoken register most consumer and SMB SaaS products aim for. The prose here is original; the underlying conventions are common professional practice, documented across public writing standards such as plainlanguage.gov and the GOV.UK style guide (see sources).

voice.identity: A knowledgeable colleague talking a busy person through their own work — direct, warm, and specific. The product speaks like one competent human, not like a brand campaign and not like a terms-of-service document.

attributes.name: Direct
attributes.description: Say the thing. Lead with the point, keep sentences short, and cut every word that exists only to sound professional.

attributes.name: Warm without performing
attributes.description: Friendliness comes from being helpful and unhurried, not from exclamation marks. One genuine sentence beats three enthusiastic ones.

attributes.name: Concrete
attributes.description: Name the object, the amount, the date, the next step. Vague copy reads as either evasive or unfinished.

attributes.name: Respectful of attention
attributes.description: Assume the reader is mid-task. Front-load meaning, keep lines scannable, and never make someone read a paragraph to find the button.

attributes.name: Calm under failure
attributes.description: When something breaks, the voice gets quieter, not cuter. State the problem and the next move; playfulness disappears entirely.

tone_shifts.onboarding: Encouraging and momentum-building. Get the person to a first concrete win quickly; skip the tour of everything the product can theoretically do.
tone_shifts.success: Brief and genuine. A short confirmation in everyday language, then step aside — or point at one sensible follow-up.
tone_shifts.errors: Plain, steady, useful. The problem, the reason when the reason changes their next move, and the way forward. No jokes, no fault-finding, no drawn-out apologizing.
tone_shifts.billing-and-legal: Slightly more formal and completely unambiguous. Every figure, date, and currency has to land correctly on the first read. Humor never appears here.
tone_shifts.empty-states: Instructive and forward-looking. Explain the screen's purpose, preview the content that activity will bring, and end on a single obvious action.

avoid: delight (as a verb aimed at the user)
simply / just (minimizers that read as condescension when the task isn't simple)
never: Internal codenames or schema names anywhere a customer can see them
An acronym before its full form has appeared once
Trend-chasing slang — it ages fast and excludes non-native speakers
Idioms or cultural references tied to a single country; state the underlying meaning directly

grammar.voice: Active voice with a named actor. 'You're out of storage' — not 'The storage limit has been reached.'
grammar.contractions: Written-out forms sound robotic; it's, you're, and we'll are how people talk. The one exception is legal text, where precision outranks warmth.
grammar.person: The reader is 'you'; the company is 'we'. The phrase 'the user' belongs in specs, not on screens.
grammar.titles: Sentence case everywhere — headings, page titles, buttons. Capitals are reserved for proper nouns and product names.
grammar.numbers: Single-digit counts appear as words; from 10 upward, numerals. Money, percentages, measurements, and clock times are numerals at any size.
grammar.abbreviations: Give the full form the first time a term appears, then the short form. Acronyms carry no internal periods.
grammar.dates-and-times: Name the month and attach a time zone — 'March 4, 2026 at 2:00 pm ET'. An all-numeric date is read differently on each side of the Atlantic.

errors.structure: The problem, stated in the reader's terms, followed by the way forward. Include the cause only when it changes their decision. Never assign fault, never surface internals.
errors.example-good: We couldn't save your changes — your session expired. Sign in again and your draft will still be here.

empty-states.structure: Purpose of the screen → the content activity will bring → a single action to get started.
empty-states.example-good: Nothing exported yet. Reports you export will be listed here. Export your first report.

success.structure: A specific confirmation, plus a follow-up action when a natural one exists — otherwise nothing more.
success.example-good: Your report is scheduled for Monday at 9:00 am ET. We'll email you when it's ready.

rules: Short enough to scan: under five words
Use 'they/them' when a person's gender is unknown.
Describe what a feature does, not who it is for — 'compatible with screen readers' rather than ability-based shorthand.
Swap disability metaphors for the literal meaning: 'gap' for 'blind spot', 'out of touch' for 'tone-deaf'.
Where an idiom assumes one culture, state its meaning plainly.
Make no assumptions about family structure, employment type, or physical ability.
